meta.review_notes: Policy is silent on camera/microphone, location, contacts, storage access, and payment handling. Several categories marked unknown. Facebook ID collection is automatic and unexplained.

app.name: Muscle Monster Workout Planner
app.description: A workout planner app that helps users schedule practice sessions, track progress, and set body improvement goals.

verdict.one_liner: Collects workout and health data plus your Facebook ID, but promises never to sell your information.
verdict.summary: Muscle Monster gathers your practice schedule, body goals, and how you feel after workouts, along with your Facebook ID and device information. The developer explicitly promises never to sell your data and limits sharing to aggregated, non-identifying information. However, several important privacy categories like location, camera, and contacts are not addressed in the policy, leaving gaps in transparency.
verdict.recommendation_reason: The app collects meaningful health and fitness data, logs your Facebook ID automatically, and leaves major privacy categories unaddressed in its policy.

red.title: Facebook ID collected automatically
red.plain_english: The app grabs your Facebook ID without you necessarily signing in through Facebook. This is a unique identifier that can be used to track you across apps and websites.

red.title: Workout and body data stored on servers
red.plain_english: Your practice schedule, body improvement goals, and how you feel after workouts are saved on company servers. This is personal health information that could reveal sensitive details about your body and habits.

red.title: Uninstalling does not delete server data
red.plain_english: The policy says you can remove stored data by uninstalling the app, but that only deletes data on your phone. Your information likely stays on their servers unless you manually email them to request deletion.

red.title: Several privacy areas not mentioned
red.plain_english: The policy does not say anything about location tracking, camera access, contacts, or file storage. This means you cannot know whether the app uses these permissions or not.

green.title: Explicit no-sell promise
green.plain_english: The developer guarantees twice in the policy that the information they collect will never be sold. This is a strong commitment that many apps do not make.

green.title: Only shares anonymized data
green.plain_english: When they do share information with others, they only share data that has been grouped together and stripped of details that could identify you personally.

green.title: California privacy rights honored
green.plain_english: Users in California can ask to see what data the company has collected about them and request deletion of that data. You will not be treated worse for exercising these rights.

green.title: No intentional data collection from children
green.plain_english: The app says it does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 and requires users to be at least 16 years old.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: The privacy policy does not mention camera or microphone access at all, so it is unclear whether the app uses them.
categories.detail: Policy is completely silent on camera and microphone permissions. For a workout planner, camera might be used for progress photos, but this is not disclosed.
concerns: No disclosure of camera or microphone usage

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: The policy does not say whether the app tracks your location or GPS data.
categories.detail: No mention of location services, GPS tracking, or geofencing in the policy. Some workout apps use location for outdoor activity tracking, but this is not addressed.
concerns: No disclosure of location data collection or usage

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: The policy does not mention whether the app can access your phone contacts or address book.
categories.detail: No reference to contacts, phonebook, or social graph access. For a workout planner, this is likely not needed, but the absence of explicit disclosure is a transparency gap.
concerns: No disclosure of contacts access

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: The policy does not explain what files or storage areas on your phone the app can access.
categories.detail: While the app must store workout data internally, there is no disclosure about access to photos, media, downloads, or broad file system permissions.
concerns: No disclosure of file or storage access scope

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: The developer promises never to sell your data and only shares information that has been stripped of personal details or is required by law.
categories.detail: Sharing is limited to aggregated/de-identified data, legal compliance, and safety. The explicit no-sell promise is notable, though the legal exceptions are standard boilerplate.
categories.policy_excerpt: We guarantee that the information we collect will never be sold. We may share non-personal information that is aggregated or de-identified so that it cannot reasonably be used to identify an individual.
concerns: Legal compliance disclosures could be broad
Facebook SDK presence suggests possible additional sharing not disclosed

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: The app collects your practice details and preferences tied to your account, plus your Facebook ID automatically.
categories.detail: Account data includes workout schedule, body improvement areas, post-practice feelings, and preferences. The automatic collection of Facebook ID raises identity linkage concerns.
categories.policy_excerpt: This information includes: data directly/indirectly relating to your practice... and your preferences relating to the ways of improving your body. Examples of such data include... Facebook ID.
concerns: Facebook ID collected automatically without clear opt-out
Health-related preferences linked to identity

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: The app records how you tap around the interface, which features you use, and how long you stay in the app. Your Facebook ID is also collected, which can be used for tracking across apps.
categories.detail: Usage logging includes taps, feature interactions, session duration, and subscription orders. While stated purpose is product improvement, the presence of Facebook ID automatic collection suggests possible ad/analytics SDK integration not fully disclosed.
categories.policy_excerpt: We record how you interact with our Service. For example, we log your taps on certain areas of the interface, the features, and content you interact with, how often you use the App, how long you are in the App, what sections you use, and your subscription orders.
concerns: Detailed interaction logging
Facebook ID automatic collection suggests tracking SDK
No mention of whether data is used for ads

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The app says it does not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13 and requires users to be over 16.
categories.detail: Explicit age floor of 16 and COPPA/CCPA alignment for children's data. No child-directed features apparent.
categories.policy_excerpt: We do not knowingly collect Personal Data from children under the age of 13.

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: The policy does not suggest unusual tracking of your internet activity or network traffic.
categories.detail: Standard internet connectivity is required for service operation. No mention of network monitoring, traffic analysis, or proxying.

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: The app collects your device language, model, settings, operating system, and Facebook ID automatically.
categories.detail: Device data collection includes language settings, type/model, device settings, OS, and Facebook ID. While claimed purpose is bug fixing, the Facebook ID is a persistent cross-app identifier.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect data about your mobile device. Examples of such data include language settings, type and model of a device, device settings, operating system, and Facebook ID.
concerns: Facebook ID is a persistent identifier
Automatic collection without explicit opt-out
Could enable cross-app tracking

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: The app collects your workout schedule, body improvement goals, and how you feel after practice, which is personal health information.
categories.detail: Health-adjacent data includes practice schedule, post-practice feelings, body type improvement areas, and fitness preferences. Stored on servers and linked to user account.
categories.policy_excerpt: data directly/indirectly relating to your practice (including your practice schedule (i.e., time you practice), how you feel after practice, areas for improving body type, and your preferences relating to the ways of improving your body).
concerns: Health data stored on external servers
No mention of encryption or special health data safeguards

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: The app tracks subscription orders but does not claim to store your payment card details directly.
categories.detail: Subscription orders are logged as usage data, likely referring to Apple In-App Purchase transactions. No mention of direct card storage or payment processing.

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can email the developer to request deletion, but uninstalling the app alone will not remove your data from their servers.
categories.detail: Policy incorrectly implies uninstalling deletes data. CCPA deletion rights exist via email contact. No mention of automated self-service deletion or data export.
categories.policy_excerpt: You can simply uninstall the app to remove any stored data at any time. You can request the deletion of your data by contacting us at support@musclemonster.fit.
concerns: Uninstall misleadingly presented as deletion method
No automated self-service deletion
No mention of data export

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: If the privacy policy changes, they will post a notice in the app. If you keep using the app, that counts as agreeing to the new terms.
categories.detail: Standard notice-through-app approach for material changes. Continued use constitutes consent. No advance email or push notification guarantee.
categories.policy_excerpt: We will inform you of any changes by posting the updated Privacy Policy through the mobile applications... Your continued use of the Services after the changes are made will indicate your consent.
concerns: Continued use equals acceptance
No guaranteed direct notification method
